29: /// A [`tower::Service`] that abstractly represents "the rest of the network".
30: ///
31: /// This implementation is adapted from the one in `tower-balance`, and as
32: /// described in that crate's documentation, it
33: ///
34: /// > Distributes requests across inner services using the [Power of Two Choices][p2c].
35: /// >
36: /// > As described in the [Finagle Guide][finagle]:
37: /// >
38: /// > > The algorithm randomly picks two services from the set of ready endpoints and
39: /// > > selects the least loaded of the two. By repeatedly using this strategy, we can
40: /// > > expect a manageable upper bound on the maximum load of any server.
41: /// > >
42: /// > > The maximum load variance between any two servers is bound by `ln(ln(n))` where
43: /// > > `n` is the number of servers in the cluster.
44: ///
45: /// This should work well for many network requests, but not all of them: some
46: /// requests, e.g., a request for some particular inventory item, can only be
47: /// made to a subset of connected peers, e.g., the ones that have recently
48: /// advertised that inventory hash, and other requests require specialized logic
49: /// (e.g., transaction diffusion).
50: ///
51: /// Implementing this specialized routing logic inside the `PeerSet` -- so that
52: /// it continues to abstract away "the rest of the network" into one endpoint --
53: /// is not a problem, as the `PeerSet` can simply maintain more information on
54: /// its peers and route requests appropriately. However, there is a problem with
55: /// maintaining accurate backpressure information, because the `Service` trait
56: /// requires that service readiness is independent of the data in the request.
57: ///
58: /// For this reason, in the future, this code will probably be refactored to
59: /// address this backpressure mismatch. One possibility is to refactor the code
60: /// so that one entity holds and maintains the peer set and metadata on the
61: /// peers, and each "backpressure category" of request is assigned to different
62: /// `Service` impls with specialized `poll_ready()` implementations. Another
63: /// less-elegant solution (which might be useful as an intermediate step for the
64: /// inventory case) is to provide a way to borrow a particular backing service,
65: /// say by address.
66: ///
67: /// [finagle]: https://twitter.github.io/finagle/guide/Clients.html#power-of-two-choices-p2c-least-loaded
68: /// [p2c]: http://www.eecs.harvard.edu/~michaelm/postscripts/handbook2001.pdf
69: pub struct PeerSet<D>
70: where
71:     D: Discover,
72: {
73:     discover: D,
74:     ready_services: IndexMap<D::Key, D::Service>,
75:     cancel_handles: HashMap<D::Key, oneshot::Sender<()>>,
76:     unready_services: FuturesUnordered<UnreadyService<D::Key, D::Service, Request>>,
77:     next_idx: Option<usize>,
78:     demand_signal: mpsc::Sender<()>,
79: }
80: 
81: impl<D> PeerSet<D>
82: where
83:     D: Discover + Unpin,
84:     D::Key: Clone + Debug,
85:     D::Service: Service<Request, Response = Response> + Load,
86:     D::Error: Into<BoxedStdError>,
87:     <D::Service as Service<Request>>::Error: Into<BoxedStdError> + 'static,
88:     <D::Service as Service<Request>>::Future: Send + 'static,
89:     <D::Service as Load>::Metric: Debug,
90: {
91:     /// Construct a peerset which uses `discover` internally.
92:     pub fn new(discover: D, demand_signal: mpsc::Sender<()>) -> Self {
93:         Self {
94:             discover,
95:             ready_services: IndexMap::new(),
96:             cancel_handles: HashMap::new(),
97:             unready_services: FuturesUnordered::new(),
98:             next_idx: None,
99:             demand_signal,
100:         }
101:     }
102: 
103:     fn poll_discover(&mut self, cx: &mut Context<'_>) -> Poll<Result<(), BoxedStdError>> {
104:         use futures::ready;
105:         loop {
106:             match ready!(Pin::new(&mut self.discover).poll_discover(cx)).map_err(Into::into)? {
107:                 Change::Remove(key) => {
108:                     trace!(?key, "got Change::Remove from Discover");
109:                     self.remove(&key);
110:                 }
111:                 Change::Insert(key, svc) => {
112:                     trace!(?key, "got Change::Insert from Discover");
113:                     self.remove(&key);
114:                     self.push_unready(key, svc);
115:                 }
116:             }
117:         }
118:     }
119: 
120:     fn remove(&mut self, key: &D::Key) {
121:         // Remove key from either the set of ready services,
122:         // or else from the set of unready services.
123:         if let Some((i, _, _)) = self.ready_services.swap_remove_full(key) {
124:             // swap_remove perturbs the position of the last element of
125:             // ready_services, so we may have invalidated self.next_idx, in
126:             // which case we need to fix it. Specifically, swap_remove swaps the
127:             // position of the removee and the last element, then drops the
128:             // removee from the end, so we compare the active and removed indices:
129:             let len = self.ready_services.len();
130:             self.next_idx = match self.next_idx {
131:                 None => None,                   // No active index
132:                 Some(j) if j == i => None,      // We removed j
133:                 Some(j) if j == len => Some(i), // We swapped i and j
134:                 Some(j) => Some(j),             // We swapped an unrelated service.
135:             };
136:             // No Heisenservices: they must be ready or unready.
137:             debug_assert!(!self.cancel_handles.contains_key(key));
138:         } else if let Some(handle) = self.cancel_handles.remove(key) {
139:             let _ = handle.send(());
140:         }
141:     }
142: 
143:     fn push_unready(&mut self, key: D::Key, svc: D::Service) {
144:         let (tx, rx) = oneshot::channel();
145:         self.cancel_handles.insert(key.clone(), tx);
146:         self.unready_services.push(UnreadyService {
147:             key: Some(key),
148:             service: Some(svc),
149:             cancel: rx,
150:             _req: PhantomData,
151:         });
152:     }
153: 
154:     fn poll_unready(&mut self, cx: &mut Context<'_>) {
155:         loop {
156:             match Pin::new(&mut self.unready_services).poll_next(cx) {
157:                 Poll::Pending | Poll::Ready(None) => return,
158:                 Poll::Ready(Some(Ok((key, svc)))) => {
159:                     trace!(?key, "service became ready");
160:                     let _cancel = self.cancel_handles.remove(&key);
161:                     debug_assert!(_cancel.is_some(), "missing cancel handle");
162:                     self.ready_services.insert(key, svc);
163:                 }
164:                 Poll::Ready(Some(Err((key, UnreadyError::Canceled)))) => {
165:                     debug_assert!(!self.cancel_handles.contains_key(&key))
166:                 }
167:                 Poll::Ready(Some(Err((key, UnreadyError::Inner(e))))) => {
168:                     let error = e.into();
169:                     debug!(%error, "service failed while unready, dropped");
170:                     let _cancel = self.cancel_handles.remove(&key);
171:                     debug_assert!(_cancel.is_some(), "missing cancel handle");
172:                 }
173:             }
174:         }
175:     }
176: 
177:     /// Performs P2C on inner services to select a ready service.
178:     fn select_next_ready_index(&mut self) -> Option<usize> {
179:         match self.ready_services.len() {
180:             0 => None,
181:             1 => Some(0),
182:             len => {
183:                 // XXX avoid relying on rand complexity
184:                 let (a, b) = {
185:                     let idxs = rand::seq::index::sample(&mut rand::thread_rng(), len, 2);
186:                     (idxs.index(0), idxs.index(1))
187:                 };
188: 
189:                 let a_load = self.ready_index_load(a);
190:                 let b_load = self.ready_index_load(b);
191: 
192:                 let selected = if a_load <= b_load { a } else { b };
193: 
194:                 trace!(a.idx = a, a.load = ?a_load, b.idx = b, b.load = ?b_load, selected, "selected service by p2c");
195: 
196:                 Some(selected)
197:             }
198:         }
199:     }
200: 
201:     /// Accesses a ready endpoint by index and returns its current load.
202:     fn ready_index_load(&self, index: usize) -> <D::Service as Load>::Metric {
203:         let (_, svc) = self.ready_services.get_index(index).expect("invalid index");
204:         svc.load()
205:     }
206: }
207: 
208: impl<D> Service<Request> for PeerSet<D>
209: where
210:     D: Discover + Unpin,
211:     D::Key: Clone + Debug,
212:     D::Service: Service<Request, Response = Response> + Load,
213:     D::Error: Into<BoxedStdError>,
214:     <D::Service as Service<Request>>::Error: Into<BoxedStdError> + 'static,
215:     <D::Service as Service<Request>>::Future: Send + 'static,
216:     <D::Service as Load>::Metric: Debug,
217: {
218:     type Response = Response;
219:     type Error = BoxedStdError;
220:     type Future =
221:         Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = Result<Self::Response, Self::Error>> + Send + 'static>>;
222: 
223:     fn poll_ready(&mut self, cx: &mut Context<'_>) -> Poll<Result<(), Self::Error>> {
224:         // Process peer discovery updates.
225:         let _ = self.poll_discover(cx)?;
226: 
227:         // Poll unready services to drive them to readiness.
228:         self.poll_unready(cx);
229:         trace!(
230:             num_ready = self.ready_services.len(),
231:             num_unready = self.unready_services.len(),
232:         );
233: 
234:         loop {
235:             // Re-check that the pre-selected service is ready, in case
236:             // something has happened since (e.g., it failed, peer closed
237:             // connection, ...)
238:             if let Some(index) = self.next_idx {
239:                 let (key, service) = self
240:                     .ready_services
241:                     .get_index_mut(index)
242:                     .expect("preselected index must be valid");
243:                 trace!(preselected_index = index, ?key);
244:                 match service.poll_ready(cx) {
245:                     Poll::Ready(Ok(())) => return Poll::Ready(Ok(())),
246:                     Poll::Pending => {
247:                         trace!("preselected service is no longer ready");
248:                         let (key, service) = self
249:                             .ready_services
250:                             .swap_remove_index(index)
251:                             .expect("preselected index must be valid");
252:                         self.push_unready(key, service);
253:                     }
254:                     Poll::Ready(Err(e)) => {
255:                         let error = e.into();
256:                         trace!(%error, "preselected service failed, dropping it");
257:                         self.ready_services
258:                             .swap_remove_index(index)
259:                             .expect("preselected index must be valid");
260:                     }
261:                 }
262:             }
263: 
264:             trace!("preselected service was not ready, reselecting");
265:             self.next_idx = self.select_next_ready_index();
266: 
267:             if self.next_idx.is_none() {
268:                 trace!("no ready services, sending demand signal");
269:                 let _ = self.demand_signal.try_send(());
270:                 return Poll::Pending;
271:             }
272:         }
273:     }
274: 
275:     fn call(&mut self, req: Request) -> Self::Future {
276:         let index = self
277:             .next_idx
278:             .take()
279:             .expect("ready service must have valid preselected index");
280:         let (key, mut svc) = self
281:             .ready_services
282:             .swap_remove_index(index)
283:             .expect("preselected index must be valid");
284: 
285:         let fut = svc.call(req);
286:         self.push_unready(key, svc);
287: 
288:         use futures::future::TryFutureExt;
289:         fut.map_err(Into::into).boxed()

37: /// Initialize a peer set with the given `config`, forwarding peer requests to the `inbound_service`.

40:     inbound_service: S,
41: ) -> (
42:     impl Service<
43:             Request,
44:             Response = Response,
45:             Error = BoxedStdError,
46:             Future = impl Future<Output = Result<Response, BoxedStdError>> + Send,
47:         > + Send
48:         + Clone
49:         + 'static,

54:     S::Future: Send + 'static,

56:     let (address_book, timestamp_collector) = TimestampCollector::spawn();
57: 
58:     // Construct services that handle inbound handshakes and perform outbound
59:     // handshakes. These use the same handshake service internally to detect
60:     // self-connection attempts. Both are decorated with a tower TimeoutLayer to
61:     // enforce timeouts as specified in the Config.
62:     let (listener, connector) = {
63:         use tower::timeout::TimeoutLayer;
64:         let hs_timeout = TimeoutLayer::new(config.handshake_timeout);
65:         let hs = peer::Handshake::new(config.clone(), inbound_service, timestamp_collector);
66:         (
67:             hs_timeout.layer(hs.clone()),
68:             hs_timeout.layer(peer::Connector::new(hs)),
69:         )
70:     };
71: 
72:     // Create an mpsc channel for peer changes, with a generous buffer.
73:     let (peerset_tx, peerset_rx) = mpsc::channel::<PeerChange>(100);
74:     // Create an mpsc channel for peerset demand signaling.
75:     let (demand_tx, demand_rx) = mpsc::channel::<()>(100);
76: 
77:     // Connect the rx end to a PeerSet, wrapping new peers in load instruments.
78:     let peer_set = Buffer::new(
79:         PeerSet::new(
80:             PeakEwmaDiscover::new(
81:                 ServiceStream::new(
82:                     // ServiceStream interprets an error as stream termination,
83:                     // so discard any errored connections...
84:                     peerset_rx.filter(|result| future::ready(result.is_ok())),
85:                 ),
86:                 config.ewma_default_rtt,
87:                 config.ewma_decay_time,
88:                 NoInstrument,
89:             ),
90:             demand_tx,
91:         ),
92:         config.peerset_request_buffer_size,
93:     );

97:     // 1. Initial peers, specified in the config.

101:         peerset_tx.clone(),
102:     ));

104:     // 2. Incoming peer connections, via a listener.
105:     tokio::spawn(
106:         listen(config.listen_addr, listener, peerset_tx.clone()).map(|result| {
107:             if let Err(e) = result {
108:                 error!(%e);
109:             }
110:         }),
111:     );

142: /// Use the provided `handshaker` to connect to `initial_peers`, then send
143: /// the results over `tx`.

146:     initial_peers: Vec<SocketAddr>,
147:     connector: S,
148:     mut tx: mpsc::Sender<PeerChange>,

150:     S: Service<SocketAddr, Response = Change<SocketAddr, peer::Client>, Error = BoxedStdError>
151:         + Clone,

154:     info!(?initial_peers, "Connecting to initial peer set");
155:     use tower::util::CallAllUnordered;
156:     let addr_stream = futures::stream::iter(initial_peers.into_iter());
157:     let mut handshakes = CallAllUnordered::new(connector, addr_stream);
158:     while let Some(handshake_result) = handshakes.next().await {

168:     mut handshaker: S,

211:     use futures::TryFutureExt;

213:     // On creation, we are likely to have very few peers, so try to get more
214:     // connections quickly by concurrently connecting to a large number of
215:     // candidates.

230:         match handshake {

234:             }

236:                 debug!(?candidate.addr, "marking address as failed");

238:             }
239:         }
240:     }

243:         tokio::time::interval(new_peer_interval).map(|_| ()),
244:         demand_signal,
245:     );

247:         debug!("got demand signal from peer set, updating candidates");
248:         candidates.update().await?;
249:         loop {

251:                 Some(candidate) => candidate,

258:             connector.ready().await?;

3: /// A "retry policy" to classify if a request should be retried.
4: ///
5: /// # Example
6: ///
7: /// ```
8: /// use tower_retry::Policy;
9: /// use futures_util::future;
10: ///
11: /// type Req = String;
12: /// type Res = String;
13: ///
14: /// struct Attempts(usize);
15: ///
16: /// impl<E> Policy<Req, Res, E> for Attempts {
17: ///     type Future = future::Ready<Self>;
18: ///
19: ///     fn retry(&self, req: &Req, result: Result<&Res, &E>) -> Option<Self::Future> {
20: ///         match result {
21: ///             Ok(_) => {
22: ///                 // Treat all `Response`s as success,
23: ///                 // so don't retry...
24: ///                 None
25: ///             },
26: ///             Err(_) => {
27: ///                 // Treat all errors as failures...
28: ///                 // But we limit the number of attempts...
29: ///                 if self.0 > 0 {
30: ///                     // Try again!
31: ///                     Some(future::ready(Attempts(self.0 - 1)))
32: ///                 } else {
33: ///                     // Used all our attempts, no retry...
34: ///                     None
35: ///                 }
36: ///             }
37: ///         }
38: ///     }
39: ///
40: ///     fn clone_request(&self, req: &Req) -> Option<Req> {
41: ///         Some(req.clone())
42: ///     }
43: /// }
44: /// ```
45: pub trait Policy<Req, Res, E>: Sized {
46:     /// The `Future` type returned by `Policy::retry()`.
47:     type Future: Future<Output = Self>;
48:     /// Check the policy if a certain request should be retried.
49:     ///
50:     /// This method is passed a reference to the original request, and either
51:     /// the `Service::Response` or `Service::Error` from the inner service.
52:     ///
53:     /// If the request should **not** be retried, return `None`.
54:     ///
55:     /// If the request *should* be retried, return `Some` future of a new
56:     /// policy that would apply for the next request attempt.
57:     fn retry(&self, req: &Req, result: Result<&Res, &E>) -> Option<Self::Future>;
58:     /// Tries to clone a request before being passed to the inner service.
59:     ///
60:     /// If the request cannot be cloned, return `None`.
61:     fn clone_request(&self, req: &Req) -> Option<Req>;
62: }

14: /// The number of times a request should be retried after a failure.

23: /// A [`tower::retry::Policy`] which retries requests that fail, up to a

26: /// Each new policy is constructed from the previous one, decrementing the

28: /// configured number of times before its failure is returned to the caller.

30: pub struct Retry<Req> {

35:     _service: PhantomData<Req>,
36: }

44:         }

66:                 RetryLimit::Count(n) => {

1: //! Serialization for Zcash.
2: //!
3: //! This module contains four traits: `ZcashSerialize` and `ZcashDeserialize`,
4: //! analogs of the Serde `Serialize` and `Deserialize` traits but intended for
5: //! consensus-critical Zcash serialization formats, and `WriteZcashExt` and
6: //! `ReadZcashExt`, extension traits for `io::Read` and `io::Write` with utility functions
7: //! for reading and writing data (e.g., the Bitcoin variable-integer format).
8: 
9: use std::io;
10: use std::net::{IpAddr, SocketAddr};
11: 
12: use byteorder::{BigEndian, LittleEndian, ReadBytesExt, WriteBytesExt};
13: use thiserror::Error;
14: 
15: /// A serialization error.
16: // XXX refine error types -- better to use boxed errors?
17: #[derive(Error, Debug)]
18: pub enum SerializationError {
19:     /// An underlying IO error.
20:     #[error("io error")]
21:     Io(#[from] io::Error),
22:     /// The data to be deserialized was malformed.
23:     // XXX refine errors
24:     #[error("parse error: {0}")]
25:     Parse(&'static str),
26: }

28: /// Consensus-critical serialization for Zcash.
29: ///
30: /// This trait provides a generic serialization for consensus-critical
31: /// formats, such as network messages, transactions, blocks, etc. It is intended
32: /// for use only in consensus-critical contexts; in other contexts, such as
33: /// internal storage, it would be preferable to use Serde.
34: ///
35: /// This trait can only fail if the underlying `writer` fails, so it is safe
36: /// to use in contexts (such as hashing) where the serialized bytes must
37: /// always be available. Implementations MUST NOT return an error for invalid
38: /// data, since that would make it impossible to serialize e.g. typed hashes.
39: /// Instead, any value whose representation cannot be serialized should be
40: /// made unrepresentable by the type itself.
41: pub trait ZcashSerialize: Sized {
42:     /// Write `self` to the given `writer` using the canonical format.
43:     ///
44:     /// This function has a `zcash_` prefix to alert the reader that the
45:     /// serialization in use is consensus-critical serialization, rather than
46:     /// some other kind of serialization.
47:     ///
48:     /// This function is infallible, except for errors in the underlying
49:     /// `writer`, so serialization of any data into a hash is always possible.
50:     fn zcash_serialize<W: io::Write>(&self, writer: W) -> Result<(), io::Error>;
51: }
52: 
53: /// Consensus-critical serialization for Zcash.
54: ///
55: /// This trait provides a generic deserialization for consensus-critical
56: /// formats, such as network messages, transactions, blocks, etc. It is intended
57: /// for use only in consensus-critical contexts; in other contexts, such as
58: /// internal storage, it would be preferable to use Serde.
59: pub trait ZcashDeserialize: Sized {
60:     /// Try to read `self` from the given `reader`.
61:     ///
62:     /// This function has a `zcash_` prefix to alert the reader that the
63:     /// serialization in use is consensus-critical serialization, rather than
64:     /// some other kind of serialization.
65:     fn zcash_deserialize<R: io::Read>(reader: R) -> Result<Self, SerializationError>;
66: }
67: 
68: impl<T: ZcashSerialize> ZcashSerialize for Vec<T> {
69:     fn zcash_serialize<W: io::Write>(&self, mut writer: W) -> Result<(), io::Error> {
70:         writer.write_compactsize(self.len() as u64)?;
71:         for x in self {
72:             x.zcash_serialize(&mut writer)?;
73:         }
74:         Ok(())
75:     }
76: }
77: 
78: impl<T: ZcashDeserialize> ZcashDeserialize for Vec<T> {
79:     fn zcash_deserialize<R: io::Read>(mut reader: R) -> Result<Self, SerializationError> {
80:         let len = reader.read_compactsize()?;
81:         // We're given len, so we could preallocate. But blindly preallocating
82:         // without a size bound can allow DOS attacks, and there's no way to
83:         // pass a size bound in a ZcashDeserialize impl, so instead we allocate
84:         // as we read from the reader.
85:         let mut vec = Vec::new();
86:         for _ in 0..len {
87:             vec.push(T::zcash_deserialize(&mut reader)?);
88:         }
89:         Ok(vec)
90:     }
91: }

93: /// Extends [`Write`] with methods for writing Zcash/Bitcoin types.
94: ///
95: /// [`Write`]: https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/io/trait.Write.html
96: pub trait WriteZcashExt: io::Write {
97:     /// Writes a `u64` using the Bitcoin `CompactSize` encoding.
98:     ///
99:     /// # Examples
100:     ///
101:     /// ```rust
102:     /// use zebra_chain::serialization::WriteZcashExt;
103:     ///
104:     /// let mut buf = Vec::new();
105:     /// buf.write_compactsize(0x12).unwrap();
106:     /// assert_eq!(buf, b"\x12");
107:     ///
108:     /// let mut buf = Vec::new();
109:     /// buf.write_compactsize(0xfd).unwrap();
110:     /// assert_eq!(buf, b"\xfd\xfd\x00");
111:     ///
112:     /// let mut buf = Vec::new();
113:     /// buf.write_compactsize(0xaafd).unwrap();
114:     /// assert_eq!(buf, b"\xfd\xfd\xaa");
115:     ///
116:     /// let mut buf = Vec::new();
117:     /// buf.write_compactsize(0xbbaafd).unwrap();
118:     /// assert_eq!(buf, b"\xfe\xfd\xaa\xbb\x00");
119:     ///
120:     /// let mut buf = Vec::new();
121:     /// buf.write_compactsize(0x22ccbbaafd).unwrap();
122:     /// assert_eq!(buf, b"\xff\xfd\xaa\xbb\xcc\x22\x00\x00\x00");
123:     /// ```
124:     #[inline]
125:     fn write_compactsize(&mut self, n: u64) -> io::Result<()> {
126:         match n {
127:             0x0000_0000..=0x0000_00fc => self.write_u8(n as u8),
128:             0x0000_00fd..=0x0000_ffff => {
129:                 self.write_u8(0xfd)?;
130:                 self.write_u16::<LittleEndian>(n as u16)
131:             }
132:             0x0001_0000..=0xffff_ffff => {
133:                 self.write_u8(0xfe)?;
134:                 self.write_u32::<LittleEndian>(n as u32)
135:             }
136:             _ => {
137:                 self.write_u8(0xff)?;
138:                 self.write_u64::<LittleEndian>(n)
139:             }
140:         }
141:     }

144:     #[inline]
145:     fn write_ip_addr(&mut self, addr: IpAddr) -> io::Result<()> {
146:         use std::net::IpAddr::*;
147:         let v6_addr = match addr {
148:             V4(ref v4) => v4.to_ipv6_mapped(),
149:             V6(v6) => v6,
150:         };
151:         self.write_all(&v6_addr.octets())
152:     }

154:     /// Write a `SocketAddr` in Bitcoin format.
155:     #[inline]
156:     fn write_socket_addr(&mut self, addr: SocketAddr) -> io::Result<()> {
157:         self.write_ip_addr(addr.ip())?;
158:         self.write_u16::<BigEndian>(addr.port())
159:     }

161:     /// Write a string in Bitcoin format.
162:     #[inline]
163:     fn write_string(&mut self, string: &str) -> io::Result<()> {
164:         self.write_compactsize(string.len() as u64)?;
165:         self.write_all(string.as_bytes())
166:     }
167: }

We need to make several improvements to the networking layer to enhance peer discovery, connection reliability, and observability. The current implementation has several limitations:

    1. **Peer discovery stalls**: When the peer set runs out of candidate peers to connect to, it simply logs a warning and stops trying. This can leave the node under-connected, especially during initial startup or when many peers are unreachable.

    2. **Connection handling blocks**: Handshake futures are driven inline, which can cause delays in processing other network events. We should spawn handshake tasks to allow concurrent connection attempts.

    3. **Limited metrics**: The current metrics for the peer set and message flow are insufficient for debugging network issues. We need metrics for inbound/outbound messages and more detailed peer pool gauges.

    4. **Request failures are not retried**: The `connect` testing command doesn't retry failed requests, making it brittle when peers are slow or transiently fail.

    5. **Hash debugging is awkward**: Zcash protocol prints hash digests in reversed byte order compared to our internal Debug output. Comparing our output with other tools requires manual byte reversal.

    6. **Tuning parameters need adjustment**: The default peer connection interval (120s) and request buffer size (1) are too conservative for good network responsiveness.

    The goal is to improve the network layer's robustness, make it easier to diagnose issues, and provide better tooling for developers working with Zcash data.

## Environment Setup
Check the following configuration files to understand the build and test setup:
    - Cargo.toml (workspace root)
    - zebra-network/Cargo.toml
    - zebrad/Cargo.toml
    - zebra-chain/Cargo.toml
    - README.md (for general build instructions)

## Implementation Plan
- Update peer discovery logic to refresh the candidate set and re-trigger connection attempts when no candidates are immediately available, instead of just logging and waiting.
    - Spawn handshake futures as independent tokio tasks so multiple connection attempts can proceed concurrently without blocking the main peer management loop.
    - Add metrics counters for inbound and outbound network messages, tagging them with peer address, and add gauges for ready/unready/total peer counts in the peer set.
    - Wrap the peer service in the `connect` command with a retry policy so transient failures don't terminate the request loop.
    - Add a new `zebrad revhex` subcommand that reverses the byte order of a hex string, making it easy to compare hash Debug output with Zcash tooling that prints hashes in reversed order.
    - Tune default network parameters: reduce the peer connection interval from 120s to 60s, and increase the peerset request buffer size from 1 to 10 for better throughput.

10: /// The `CandidateSet` maintains a pool of candidate peers.
11: ///
12: /// It divides the set of all possible candidate peers into three disjoint subsets:
13: ///
14: /// 1. Disconnected peers, which we previously connected to but are not currently connected to;
15: /// 2. Gossiped peers, which we learned about from other peers but have never connected to;
16: /// 3. Failed peers, to whom we attempted to connect but were unable to.
17: ///

19: ///                         ┌─────────────────┐

23: ///                                  │

25: ///                                  │
26: ///                                  │
27: ///                                  ▼

77: pub(super) struct CandidateSet<S> {
78:     pub(super) disconnected: AddressBook,
79:     pub(super) gossiped: AddressBook,
80:     pub(super) failed: AddressBook,
81:     pub(super) peer_set: Arc<Mutex<AddressBook>>,

85: impl<S> CandidateSet<S>
86: where
87:     S: Service<Request, Response = Response, Error = BoxedStdError>,
88:     S::Future: Send + 'static,
89: {
90:     pub fn new(peer_set: Arc<Mutex<AddressBook>>, peer_service: S) -> CandidateSet<S> {
91:         CandidateSet {
92:             disconnected: AddressBook::new(span!(Level::TRACE, "disconnected peers")),
93:             gossiped: AddressBook::new(span!(Level::TRACE, "gossiped peers")),
94:             failed: AddressBook::new(span!(Level::TRACE, "failed peers")),
95:             peer_set,
96:             peer_service,
97:         }
98:     }
99: 
100:     pub async fn update(&mut self) -> Result<(), BoxedStdError> {
101:         // Opportunistically crawl the network on every update call to ensure
102:         // we're actively fetching peers. Continue independently of whether we
103:         // actually receive any peers, but always ask the network for more.
104:         // Because requests are load-balanced across existing peers, we can make
105:         // multiple requests concurrently, which will be randomly assigned to
106:         // existing peers, but we don't make too many because update may be
107:         // called while the peer set is already loaded.
108:         let mut responses = FuturesUnordered::new();
109:         for _ in 0..2usize {
110:             self.peer_service.ready().await?;
111:             responses.push(self.peer_service.call(Request::GetPeers));
112:         }
113:         while let Some(rsp) = responses.next().await {
114:             if let Ok(Response::Peers(addrs)) = rsp {
115:                 let addr_len = addrs.len();
116:                 let prev_len = self.gossiped.len();
117:                 // Filter new addresses to ensure that gossiped
118:                 let failed = &self.failed;
119:                 let peer_set = &self.peer_set;
120:                 let new_addrs = addrs
121:                     .into_iter()
122:                     .filter(|meta| !failed.contains_addr(&meta.addr))
123:                     .filter(|meta| !peer_set.lock().unwrap().contains_addr(&meta.addr));
124:                 self.gossiped.extend(new_addrs);
125:                 trace!(
126:                     addr_len,
127:                     new_addrs = self.gossiped.len() - prev_len,
128:                     "got response to GetPeers"
129:                 );
130:             } else {
131:                 trace!("got error in GetPeers request");
132:             }
133:         }
134: 
135:         // Determine whether any known peers have recently disconnected.
136:         let failed = &self.failed;
137:         let peer_set = &self.peer_set;
138:         self.disconnected.extend(
139:             peer_set
140:                 .lock()
141:                 .expect("mutex must be unpoisoned")
142:                 .disconnected_peers()
143:                 .filter(|meta| failed.contains_addr(&meta.addr)),
144:         );
145: 
146:         Ok(())
147:     }
148: 
149:     pub fn next(&mut self) -> Option<MetaAddr> {
150:         let guard = self.peer_set.lock().unwrap();
151:         self.disconnected
152:             .drain_oldest()
153:             .chain(self.gossiped.drain_newest())
154:             .chain(self.failed.drain_oldest())
155:             .filter(|meta| !guard.is_potentially_connected(&meta.addr))
156:             .next()
157:     }
158: 
159:     pub fn report_failed(&mut self, mut addr: MetaAddr) {
160:         addr.last_seen = Utc::now();
161:         self.failed.update(addr);
162:     }
163: }

38: /// Initialize a peer set with the given `config`, forwarding peer requests to the `inbound_service`.
39: pub async fn init<S>(
40:     config: Config,
41:     inbound_service: S,
42: ) -> (
43:     impl Service<
44:             Request,
45:             Response = Response,
46:             Error = BoxedStdError,
47:             Future = impl Future<Output = Result<Response, BoxedStdError>> + Send,
48:         > + Send
49:         + Clone
50:         + 'static,
51:     Arc<Mutex<AddressBook>>,
52: )
53: where
54:     S: Service<Request, Response = Response, Error = BoxedStdError> + Clone + Send + 'static,
55:     S::Future: Send + 'static,
56: {
57:     let (address_book, timestamp_collector) = TimestampCollector::spawn();
58: 
59:     // Construct services that handle inbound handshakes and perform outbound
60:     // handshakes. These use the same handshake service internally to detect
61:     // self-connection attempts. Both are decorated with a tower TimeoutLayer to
62:     // enforce timeouts as specified in the Config.
63:     let (listener, connector) = {
64:         use tower::timeout::TimeoutLayer;
65:         let hs_timeout = TimeoutLayer::new(config.handshake_timeout);
66:         let hs = peer::Handshake::new(config.clone(), inbound_service, timestamp_collector);
67:         (
68:             hs_timeout.layer(hs.clone()),
69:             hs_timeout.layer(peer::Connector::new(hs)),
70:         )
71:     };
72: 
73:     // Create an mpsc channel for peer changes, with a generous buffer.
74:     let (peerset_tx, peerset_rx) = mpsc::channel::<PeerChange>(100);
75:     // Create an mpsc channel for peerset demand signaling.
76:     let (demand_tx, demand_rx) = mpsc::channel::<()>(100);
77: 
78:     // Connect the rx end to a PeerSet, wrapping new peers in load instruments.
79:     let peer_set = Buffer::new(
80:         PeerSet::new(
81:             PeakEwmaDiscover::new(
82:                 ServiceStream::new(
83:                     // ServiceStream interprets an error as stream termination,
84:                     // so discard any errored connections...
85:                     peerset_rx.filter(|result| future::ready(result.is_ok())),
86:                 ),
87:                 config.ewma_default_rtt,
88:                 config.ewma_decay_time,
89:                 NoInstrument,
90:             ),
91:             demand_tx,
92:         ),
93:         config.peerset_request_buffer_size,
94:     );
95: 
96:     // Wrap the peer set in a retry policy, so that failed requests are handled
97:     // by retrying them (up to the configured retry limit).
98:     let peer_set = RetryLayer::new(RetryLimit::Count(config.peerset_retry_limit)).layer(peer_set);
99: 
100:     // Connect the tx end to the 3 peer sources:
101: 
102:     // 1. Initial peers, specified in the config.
103:     tokio::spawn(add_initial_peers(
104:         config.initial_peers(),
105:         connector.clone(),
106:         peerset_tx.clone(),
107:     ));
108: 
109:     // 2. Incoming peer connections, via a listener.
110:     tokio::spawn(
111:         listen(config.listen_addr, listener, peerset_tx.clone()).map(|result| {
112:             if let Err(e) = result {
113:                 error!(%e);
114:             }
115:         }),
116:     );
117: 
118:     // 3. Outgoing peers we connect to in response to load.
119: 
120:     let mut candidates = CandidateSet::new(address_book.clone(), peer_set.clone());
121: 
122:     // We need to await candidates.update() here, because Zcashd only sends one
123:     // `addr` message per connection, and if we only have one initial peer we
124:     // need to ensure that its `addr` message is used by the crawler.
125:     // XXX this should go in CandidateSet::new, but we need init() -> Result<_,_>
126:     let _ = candidates.update().await;
127: 
128:     info!("Sending initial request for peers");
129:     tokio::spawn(
130:         crawl_and_dial(
131:             config.new_peer_interval,
132:             demand_rx,
133:             candidates,
134:             connector,
135:             peerset_tx,
136:         )
137:         .map(|result| {
138:             if let Err(e) = result {
139:                 error!(%e);
140:             }
141:         }),
142:     );
143: 
144:     (peer_set, address_book)
145: }

147: /// Use the provided `handshaker` to connect to `initial_peers`, then send
148: /// the results over `tx`.
149: #[instrument(skip(initial_peers, connector, tx))]
150: async fn add_initial_peers<S>(
151:     initial_peers: Vec<SocketAddr>,
152:     connector: S,
153:     mut tx: mpsc::Sender<PeerChange>,
154: ) where
155:     S: Service<SocketAddr, Response = Change<SocketAddr, peer::Client>, Error = BoxedStdError>
156:         + Clone,
157:     S::Future: Send + 'static,
158: {
159:     info!(?initial_peers, "Connecting to initial peer set");
160:     use tower::util::CallAllUnordered;
161:     let addr_stream = futures::stream::iter(initial_peers.into_iter());
162:     let mut handshakes = CallAllUnordered::new(connector, addr_stream);
163:     while let Some(handshake_result) = handshakes.next().await {
164:         let _ = tx.send(handshake_result).await;
165:     }
166: }
167: 
168: /// Bind to `addr`, listen for peers using `handshaker`, then send the
169: /// results over `tx`.
170: #[instrument(skip(tx, handshaker))]
171: async fn listen<S>(
172:     addr: SocketAddr,
173:     mut handshaker: S,
174:     tx: mpsc::Sender<PeerChange>,
175: ) -> Result<(), BoxedStdError>
176: where
177:     S: Service<(TcpStream, SocketAddr), Response = peer::Client, Error = BoxedStdError> + Clone,
178:     S::Future: Send + 'static,
179: {
180:     let mut listener = TcpListener::bind(addr).await?;
181:     loop {
182:         if let Ok((tcp_stream, addr)) = listener.accept().await {
183:             debug!(?addr, "got incoming connection");
184:             handshaker.ready().await?;
185:             // Construct a handshake future but do not drive it yet....
186:             let handshake = handshaker.call((tcp_stream, addr));
187:             // ... instead, spawn a new task to handle this connection
188:             let mut tx2 = tx.clone();
189:             tokio::spawn(async move {
190:                 if let Ok(client) = handshake.await {
191:                     let _ = tx2.send(Ok(Change::Insert(addr, client))).await;
192:                 }
193:             });
194:         }
195:     }
196: }

198: /// Given a channel that signals a need for new peers, try to connect to a peer
199: /// and send the resulting `peer::Client` through a channel.
200: ///
201: #[instrument(skip(new_peer_interval, demand_signal, candidates, connector, success_tx))]
202: async fn crawl_and_dial<C, S>(
203:     new_peer_interval: Duration,
204:     demand_signal: mpsc::Receiver<()>,
205:     mut candidates: CandidateSet<S>,
206:     mut connector: C,
207:     mut success_tx: mpsc::Sender<PeerChange>,
208: ) -> Result<(), BoxedStdError>
209: where
210:     C: Service<SocketAddr, Response = Change<SocketAddr, peer::Client>, Error = BoxedStdError>
211:         + Clone,
212:     C::Future: Send + 'static,
213:     S: Service<Request, Response = Response, Error = BoxedStdError>,
214:     S::Future: Send + 'static,
215: {
216:     use futures::TryFutureExt;
217: 
218:     // On creation, we are likely to have very few peers, so try to get more
219:     // connections quickly by concurrently connecting to a large number of
220:     // candidates.
221:     let mut handshakes = FuturesUnordered::new();
222:     for _ in 0..50usize {
223:         if let Some(candidate) = candidates.next() {
224:             connector.ready().await?;
225:             handshakes.push(
226:                 connector
227:                     .call(candidate.addr)
228:                     // Use map_err to tag failed connections with the MetaAddr,
229:                     // so they can be reported to the CandidateSet.
230:                     .map_err(move |_| candidate),
231:             )
232:         }
233:     }
234:     while let Some(handshake) = handshakes.next().await {
235:         match handshake {
236:             Ok(change) => {
237:                 debug!("Successfully dialed new peer, sending to peerset");
238:                 success_tx.send(Ok(change)).await?;
239:             }
240:             Err(candidate) => {
241:                 debug!(?candidate.addr, "marking address as failed");
242:                 candidates.report_failed(candidate);
243:             }
244:         }
245:     }
246: 
247:     let mut connect_signal = futures::stream::select(
248:         tokio::time::interval(new_peer_interval).map(|_| ()),
249:         demand_signal,
250:     );
251:     while let Some(()) = connect_signal.next().await {
252:         debug!("got demand signal from peer set, updating candidates");
253:         candidates.update().await?;
254:         loop {
255:             let candidate = match candidates.next() {
256:                 Some(candidate) => candidate,
257:                 None => {
258:                     warn!("got demand for more peers but no available candidates");
259:                     break;
260:                 }
261:             };
262: 
263:             connector.ready().await?;
264:             match connector
265:                 .call(candidate.addr)
266:                 .map_err(move |_| candidate)
267:                 .await
268:             {
269:                 Ok(change) => {
270:                     debug!("Successfully dialed new peer, sending to peerset");
271:                     success_tx.send(Ok(change)).await?;
272:                     break;
273:                 }
274:                 Err(candidate) => {
275:                     debug!(?candidate.addr, "marking address as failed");
276:                     candidates.report_failed(candidate);
277:                 }
278:             }
279:         }
280:     }
281:     Ok(())
282: }

29: /// A [`tower::Service`] that abstractly represents "the rest of the network".
30: ///
31: /// This implementation is adapted from the one in `tower-balance`, and as
32: /// described in that crate's documentation, it
33: ///
34: /// > Distributes requests across inner services using the [Power of Two Choices][p2c].
35: /// >
36: /// > As described in the [Finagle Guide][finagle]:
37: /// >
38: /// > > The algorithm randomly picks two services from the set of ready endpoints and
39: /// > > selects the least loaded of the two. By repeatedly using this strategy, we can
40: /// > > expect a manageable upper bound on the maximum load of any server.
41: /// > >
42: /// > > The maximum load variance between any two servers is bound by `ln(ln(n))` where
43: /// > > `n` is the number of servers in the cluster.
44: ///
45: /// This should work well for many network requests, but not all of them: some
46: /// requests, e.g., a request for some particular inventory item, can only be
47: /// made to a subset of connected peers, e.g., the ones that have recently
48: /// advertised that inventory hash, and other requests require specialized logic
49: /// (e.g., transaction diffusion).
50: ///
51: /// Implementing this specialized routing logic inside the `PeerSet` -- so that
52: /// it continues to abstract away "the rest of the network" into one endpoint --
53: /// is not a problem, as the `PeerSet` can simply maintain more information on
54: /// its peers and route requests appropriately. However, there is a problem with
55: /// maintaining accurate backpressure information, because the `Service` trait
56: /// requires that service readiness is independent of the data in the request.
57: ///
58: /// For this reason, in the future, this code will probably be refactored to
59: /// address this backpressure mismatch. One possibility is to refactor the code
60: /// so that one entity holds and maintains the peer set and metadata on the
61: /// peers, and each "backpressure category" of request is assigned to different
62: /// `Service` impls with specialized `poll_ready()` implementations. Another
63: /// less-elegant solution (which might be useful as an intermediate step for the
64: /// inventory case) is to provide a way to borrow a particular backing service,
65: /// say by address.
66: ///
67: /// [finagle]: https://twitter.github.io/finagle/guide/Clients.html#power-of-two-choices-p2c-least-loaded
68: /// [p2c]: http://www.eecs.harvard.edu/~michaelm/postscripts/handbook2001.pdf
69: pub struct PeerSet<D>
70: where
71:     D: Discover,
72: {
73:     discover: D,
74:     ready_services: IndexMap<D::Key, D::Service>,
75:     cancel_handles: HashMap<D::Key, oneshot::Sender<()>>,
76:     unready_services: FuturesUnordered<UnreadyService<D::Key, D::Service, Request>>,
77:     next_idx: Option<usize>,

86:     D::Error: Into<BoxedStdError>,
87:     <D::Service as Service<Request>>::Error: Into<BoxedStdError> + 'static,
88:     <D::Service as Service<Request>>::Future: Send + 'static,
89:     <D::Service as Load>::Metric: Debug,
90: {
91:     /// Construct a peerset which uses `discover` internally.
92:     pub fn new(discover: D, demand_signal: mpsc::Sender<()>) -> Self {
93:         Self {
94:             discover,
95:             ready_services: IndexMap::new(),
96:             cancel_handles: HashMap::new(),
97:             unready_services: FuturesUnordered::new(),
98:             next_idx: None,
99:             demand_signal,
100:         }
101:     }
102: 
103:     fn poll_discover(&mut self, cx: &mut Context<'_>) -> Poll<Result<(), BoxedStdError>> {
104:         use futures::ready;
105:         loop {
106:             match ready!(Pin::new(&mut self.discover).poll_discover(cx)).map_err(Into::into)? {
107:                 Change::Remove(key) => {
108:                     trace!(?key, "got Change::Remove from Discover");
109:                     self.remove(&key);
110:                 }
111:                 Change::Insert(key, svc) => {
112:                     trace!(?key, "got Change::Insert from Discover");
113:                     self.remove(&key);
114:                     self.push_unready(key, svc);
115:                 }
116:             }
117:         }
118:     }
119: 
120:     fn remove(&mut self, key: &D::Key) {
121:         // Remove key from either the set of ready services,
122:         // or else from the set of unready services.
123:         if let Some((i, _, _)) = self.ready_services.swap_remove_full(key) {
124:             // swap_remove perturbs the position of the last element of
125:             // ready_services, so we may have invalidated self.next_idx, in
126:             // which case we need to fix it. Specifically, swap_remove swaps the
127:             // position of the removee and the last element, then drops the
128:             // removee from the end, so we compare the active and removed indices:
129:             let len = self.ready_services.len();
130:             self.next_idx = match self.next_idx {
131:                 None => None,                   // No active index
132:                 Some(j) if j == i => None,      // We removed j
133:                 Some(j) if j == len => Some(i), // We swapped i and j
134:                 Some(j) => Some(j),             // We swapped an unrelated service.
135:             };
136:             // No Heisenservices: they must be ready or unready.
137:             debug_assert!(!self.cancel_handles.contains_key(key));
138:         } else if let Some(handle) = self.cancel_handles.remove(key) {
139:             let _ = handle.send(());
140:         }
141:     }
142: 
143:     fn push_unready(&mut self, key: D::Key, svc: D::Service) {
144:         let (tx, rx) = oneshot::channel();
145:         self.cancel_handles.insert(key.clone(), tx);
146:         self.unready_services.push(UnreadyService {
147:             key: Some(key),
148:             service: Some(svc),
149:             cancel: rx,
150:             _req: PhantomData,
151:         });
152:     }
153: 
154:     fn poll_unready(&mut self, cx: &mut Context<'_>) {
155:         loop {
156:             match Pin::new(&mut self.unready_services).poll_next(cx) {
157:                 Poll::Pending | Poll::Ready(None) => return,
158:                 Poll::Ready(Some(Ok((key, svc)))) => {
159:                     trace!(?key, "service became ready");
160:                     let _cancel = self.cancel_handles.remove(&key);
161:                     debug_assert!(_cancel.is_some(), "missing cancel handle");
162:                     self.ready_services.insert(key, svc);
163:                 }
164:                 Poll::Ready(Some(Err((key, UnreadyError::Canceled)))) => {
165:                     debug_assert!(!self.cancel_handles.contains_key(&key))
166:                 }
167:                 Poll::Ready(Some(Err((key, UnreadyError::Inner(e))))) => {
168:                     let error = e.into();
169:                     debug!(%error, "service failed while unready, dropped");
170:                     let _cancel = self.cancel_handles.remove(&key);
171:                     debug_assert!(_cancel.is_some(), "missing cancel handle");
172:                 }
173:             }
174:         }
175:     }
176: 
177:     /// Performs P2C on inner services to select a ready service.
178:     fn select_next_ready_index(&mut self) -> Option<usize> {
179:         match self.ready_services.len() {
180:             0 => None,
181:             1 => Some(0),
182:             len => {
183:                 // XXX avoid relying on rand complexity
184:                 let (a, b) = {
185:                     let idxs = rand::seq::index::sample(&mut rand::thread_rng(), len, 2);
186:                     (idxs.index(0), idxs.index(1))
187:                 };
188: 
189:                 let a_load = self.ready_index_load(a);
190:                 let b_load = self.ready_index_load(b);
191: 
192:                 let selected = if a_load <= b_load { a } else { b };
193: 
194:                 trace!(a.idx = a, a.load = ?a_load, b.idx = b, b.load = ?b_load, selected, "selected service by p2c");
195: 
196:                 Some(selected)
197:             }
198:         }
199:     }
200: 
201:     /// Accesses a ready endpoint by index and returns its current load.
202:     fn ready_index_load(&self, index: usize) -> <D::Service as Load>::Metric {
203:         let (_, svc) = self.ready_services.get_index(index).expect("invalid index");
204:         svc.load()
205:     }
206: }
207: 
208: impl<D> Service<Request> for PeerSet<D>
209: where
210:     D: Discover + Unpin,
211:     D::Key: Clone + Debug,
212:     D::Service: Service<Request, Response = Response> + Load,
213:     D::Error: Into<BoxedStdError>,
214:     <D::Service as Service<Request>>::Error: Into<BoxedStdError> + 'static,
215:     <D::Service as Service<Request>>::Future: Send + 'static,
216:     <D::Service as Load>::Metric: Debug,
217: {
218:     type Response = Response;
219:     type Error = BoxedStdError;
220:     type Future =
221:         Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = Result<Self::Response, Self::Error>> + Send + 'static>>;
222: 
223:     fn poll_ready(&mut self, cx: &mut Context<'_>) -> Poll<Result<(), Self::Error>> {
224:         // Process peer discovery updates.
225:         let _ = self.poll_discover(cx)?;
226: 
227:         // Poll unready services to drive them to readiness.
228:         self.poll_unready(cx);
229:         trace!(
230:             num_ready = self.ready_services.len(),
231:             num_unready = self.unready_services.len(),
232:         );
233: 
234:         loop {
235:             // Re-check that the pre-selected service is ready, in case
236:             // something has happened since (e.g., it failed, peer closed
237:             // connection, ...)
238:             if let Some(index) = self.next_idx {
239:                 let (key, service) = self
240:                     .ready_services
241:                     .get_index_mut(index)
242:                     .expect("preselected index must be valid");
243:                 trace!(preselected_index = index, ?key);
244:                 match service.poll_ready(cx) {
245:                     Poll::Ready(Ok(())) => return Poll::Ready(Ok(())),
246:                     Poll::Pending => {
247:                         trace!("preselected service is no longer ready");
248:                         let (key, service) = self
249:                             .ready_services
250:                             .swap_remove_index(index)
251:                             .expect("preselected index must be valid");
252:                         self.push_unready(key, service);
253:                     }
254:                     Poll::Ready(Err(e)) => {
255:                         let error = e.into();
256:                         trace!(%error, "preselected service failed, dropping it");
257:                         self.ready_services
258:                             .swap_remove_index(index)
259:                             .expect("preselected index must be valid");
260:                     }
261:                 }
262:             }
263: 
264:             trace!("preselected service was not ready, reselecting");
265:             self.next_idx = self.select_next_ready_index();
266: 
267:             if self.next_idx.is_none() {
268:                 trace!("no ready services, sending demand signal");
269:                 let _ = self.demand_signal.try_send(());
270:                 return Poll::Pending;
271:             }
272:         }
273:     }
274: 
275:     fn call(&mut self, req: Request) -> Self::Future {
276:         let index = self
277:             .next_idx
278:             .take()
279:             .expect("ready service must have valid preselected index");
280:         let (key, mut svc) = self
281:             .ready_services
282:             .swap_remove_index(index)
283:             .expect("preselected index must be valid");
284: 
285:         let fut = svc.call(req);
286:         self.push_unready(key, svc);
287: 
288:         use futures::future::TryFutureExt;
289:         fut.map_err(Into::into).boxed()
290:     }
291: }

1: //! Networking code for Zebra. 🦓
2: //!
3: //! The Zcash network protocol is inherited from Bitcoin, which uses a
4: //! stateful network protocol in which messages can arrive in any
5: //! order (even before a handshake is complete!), and the same message
6: //! may be a request or a response depending on context.
7: //!
8: //! This crate translates the legacy Bitcoin/Zcash network protocol
9: //! into a stateless, request-response oriented protocol defined by
10: //! the [`Request`] and [`Response`] enums, and completely
11: //! encapsulates all peer handling code behind a single
12: //! [`tower::Service`] representing "the network" which load-balances
13: //! outbound [`Request`]s over available peers.
14: //!
15: //! Each peer connection is a distinct task, which interprets incoming
16: //! Bitcoin/Zcash messages either as [`Response`]s to pending
17: //! [`Request`]s, or as an inbound [`Request`]s to an internal
18: //! [`tower::Service`] representing "this node".  All connection state
19: //! is isolated to the peer in question, so as a side effect the
20: //! design is structurally immune to the recent `ping` attack.
21: //!
22: //! Because [`tower::Service`]s provide backpressure information, we
23: //! can dynamically manage the size of the connection pool according
24: //! to inbound and outbound demand.  The inbound service can shed load
25: //! when it is not ready for requests, causing those peer connections
26: //! to close, and the outbound service can connect to additional peers
27: //! when it is overloaded.

78: where
79:     S: Service<Request, Response = Response, Error = BoxedStdError> + Clone + Send + 'static,
80:     S::Future: Send,

83:     type Error = HandshakeError;

93:

100:         // Clone these upfront, so they can be moved into the future.

102:         let internal_service = self.internal_service.clone();
103:         let timestamp_collector = self.timestamp_collector.clone();
104:         let user_agent = self.config.user_agent.clone();
105:         let network = self.config.network.clone();
106: 
107:         let fut = async move {
108:             info!("connecting to remote peer");
109: 
110:             let mut stream =
111:                 Framed::new(tcp_stream, Codec::builder().for_network(network).finish());
112: 
113:             let local_nonce = Nonce::default();
114:             nonces
115:                 .lock()
116:                 .expect("mutex should be unpoisoned")
117:                 .insert(local_nonce);
118: 
119:             let version = Message::Version {
120:                 version: constants::CURRENT_VERSION,
121:                 services: PeerServices::NODE_NETWORK,
122:                 timestamp: Utc::now(),
123:                 address_recv: (PeerServices::NODE_NETWORK, addr),
124:                 address_from: (
125:                     PeerServices::NODE_NETWORK,
126:                     "127.0.0.1:9000".parse().unwrap(),
127:                 ),
128:                 nonce: local_nonce,
129:                 user_agent,
130:                 // XXX eventually the `PeerConnector` will need to have a handle

132:                 start_height: BlockHeight(0),
133:                 relay: false,
134:             };

136:             debug!(?version, "sending initial version message");
137:             stream.send(version).await?;
138: 
139:             let remote_msg = stream
140:                 .next()
141:                 .await
142:                 .ok_or_else(|| HandshakeError::ConnectionClosed)??;
143: 
144:             // Check that we got a Version and destructure its fields into the local scope.
145:             debug!(?remote_msg, "got message from remote peer");
146:             let (remote_nonce, remote_services) = if let Message::Version {
147:                 nonce, services, ..
148:             } = remote_msg
149:             {
150:                 (nonce, services)
151:             } else {
152:                 return Err(HandshakeError::UnexpectedMessage(remote_msg));
153:             };

155:             // Check for nonce reuse, indicating self-connection.
156:             if {

159:                 // Regardless of whether we observed nonce reuse, clean up the nonce set.
160:                 locked_nonces.remove(&local_nonce);
161:                 nonce_reuse
162:             } {
163:                 return Err(HandshakeError::NonceReuse);
164:             }

167:

169:                 .next()
170:                 .await
171:                 .ok_or_else(|| HandshakeError::ConnectionClosed)??;
172:             if let Message::Verack = remote_msg {
173:                 debug!("got verack from remote peer");
174:             } else {
175:                 return Err(HandshakeError::UnexpectedMessage(remote_msg));
176:             }
177: 
178:             // XXX here is where we would set the version to the minimum of the

184:             // These channels should not be cloned more than they are

186:             let (connection_tx, connection_rx) = mpsc::channel(0);
187:             let slot = ErrorSlot::default();
188: 
189:             let client = Client {
190:                 span: connection_span.clone(),
191:                 connection_tx: connection_tx.clone(),
192:                 error_slot: slot.clone(),
193:             };
194: 
195:             let (peer_tx, peer_rx) = stream.split();

200:                 pending_request: None,

202:                 client_rx: connection_rx,

205:                 request_timer: None,

213:                             use futures::sink::SinkExt;

217:                                     services: remote_services,
218:                                     last_seen: Utc::now(),
219:                                 })
220:                                 .await;

225:                 .boxed();

227:             tokio::spawn(
228:                 connection
229:                     .run(hooked_peer_rx)
230:                     .instrument(connection_span)
231:                     .boxed(),
232:             );
233: 
234:             tokio::spawn(async move {
235:                 use futures::channel::oneshot;
236: 
237:                 use super::client::ClientRequest;
238: 
239:                 let mut connection_tx = connection_tx;
240: 
241:                 let mut interval_stream = tokio::time::interval(constants::HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL);

243:                 loop {

14: };

17: 
18: /// An address with metadata on its advertised services and last-seen time.
19: ///
20: /// [Bitcoin reference](https://en.bitcoin.it/wiki/Protocol_documentation#Network_address)
21: #[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
22: pub struct MetaAddr {
23:     /// The peer's address.
24:     pub addr: SocketAddr,
25:     /// The services advertised by the peer.
26:     pub services: PeerServices,
27:     /// When the peer was last seen.
28:     pub last_seen: DateTime<Utc>,
29: }
30: 
31: impl MetaAddr {
32:     /// Sanitize this `MetaAddr` before sending it to a remote peer.
33:     pub fn sanitize(mut self) -> MetaAddr {
34:         let interval = crate::constants::TIMESTAMP_TRUNCATION_SECONDS;
35:         let ts = self.last_seen.timestamp();
36:         self.last_seen = Utc.timestamp(ts - ts.rem_euclid(interval), 0);
37:         self
38:     }
39: }
40: 
41: impl Ord for MetaAddr {
42:     /// `MetaAddr`s are sorted newest-first, and then in an arbitrary
43:     /// but determinate total order.
44:     fn cmp(&self, other: &Self) -> Ordering {
45:         let newest_first = self.last_seen.cmp(&other.last_seen).reverse();
46:         newest_first.then_with(|| {
47:             // The remainder is meaningless as an ordering, but required so that we
48:             // have a total order on `MetaAddr` values: self and other must compare
49:             // as Ordering::Equal iff they are equal.
50:             use std::net::IpAddr::{V4, V6};
51:             match (self.addr.ip(), other.addr.ip()) {
52:                 (V4(a), V4(b)) => a.octets().cmp(&b.octets()),
53:                 (V6(a), V6(b)) => a.octets().cmp(&b.octets()),
54:                 (V4(_), V6(_)) => Ordering::Less,
55:                 (V6(_), V4(_)) => Ordering::Greater,
56:             }
57:             .then(self.addr.port().cmp(&other.addr.port()))
58:             .then(self.services.bits().cmp(&other.services.bits()))
59:         })
60:     }
61: }
62: 
63: impl PartialOrd for MetaAddr {
64:     fn partial_cmp(&self, other: &Self) -> Option<Ordering> {
65:         Some(self.cmp(other))
66:     }
67: }
68: 
69: impl ZcashSerialize for MetaAddr {
70:     fn zcash_serialize<W: Write>(&self, mut writer: W) -> Result<(), io::Error> {
71:         writer.write_u32::<LittleEndian>(self.last_seen.timestamp() as u32)?;
72:         writer.write_u64::<LittleEndian>(self.services.bits())?;
73:         writer.write_socket_addr(self.addr)?;
74:         Ok(())
75:     }
76: }
77: 
78: impl ZcashDeserialize for MetaAddr {
79:     fn zcash_deserialize<R: Read>(mut reader: R) -> Result<Self, SerializationError> {
80:         Ok(MetaAddr {
81:             last_seen: Utc.timestamp(reader.read_u32::<LittleEndian>()? as i64, 0),
82:             // Discard unknown service bits.
83:             services: PeerServices::from_bits_truncate(reader.read_u64::<LittleEndian>()?),
84:             addr: reader.read_socket_addr()?,
85:         })
86:     }
87: }

1: //! Retry policies for outbound network requests.
2: //!
3: //! This module defines a simple retry policy which can be applied to a
4: //! [`tower::Service`] handle to the network, so that requests which fail due to
5: //! transient errors are automatically retried.
6: 
7: use std::{fmt::Debug, marker::PhantomData};
8: 
9: use futures::future::{self, Ready};
10: use tower::{layer::Layer, retry::Policy};
11: 
12: use crate::{BoxedStdError, Request, Response};
13: 
14: /// The number of times a request should be retried after a failure.
15: #[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
16: pub enum RetryLimit {
17:     /// Retry requests indefinitely.
18:     Unlimited,
19:     /// Retry requests, up to `n` retries after the initial attempt.
20:     Count(usize),
21: }
22: 
23: /// A [`tower::retry::Policy`] which retries requests that fail, up to a
24: /// configurable number of retries.
25: ///
26: /// Each new policy is constructed from the previous one, decrementing the
27: /// number of remaining retries, so that a request is retried at most the
28: /// configured number of times before its failure is returned to the caller.
29: #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
30: pub struct Retry<Req> {
31:     /// The number of retries which have not yet been used.
32:     retry_limit: RetryLimit,
33:     /// The type of the request, which is phantom because the policy does not
34:     /// actually inspect requests.
35:     _service: PhantomData<Req>,
36: }
37: 
38: impl<Req> Retry<Req> {
39:     /// Construct a new retry policy with the given `retry_limit`.
40:     pub fn new(retry_limit: RetryLimit) -> Self {
41:         Retry {
42:             retry_limit,
43:             _service: PhantomData,
44:         }
45:     }
46: }
47: 
48: impl<Req> Policy<Req, Response, BoxedStdError> for Retry<Req>
49: where
50:     Req: Clone,
51: {
52:     type Future = Ready<Self>;
53: 
54:     fn retry(
55:         &self,
56:         _req: &Req,
57:         result: Result<&Response, &BoxedStdError>,
58:     ) -> Option<Self::Future> {
59:         match result {
60:             // Do not retry successful responses.
61:             Ok(_) => None,
62:             // Retry failed requests according to the retry limit.
63:             Err(_) => match self.retry_limit {
64:                 RetryLimit::Unlimited => Some(future::ready(self.clone())),
65:                 RetryLimit::Count(0) => None,
66:                 RetryLimit::Count(n) => {
67:                     Some(future::ready(Retry::new(RetryLimit::Count(n - 1))))
68:                 }
69:             },
70:         }
71:     }
72: 
73:     fn clone_request(&self, req: &Req) -> Option<Req> {
74:         Some(req.clone())
75:     }
76: }
77: 
78: /// Wraps a [`Service`] in an inner retry policy.
79: ///
80: /// This can be used to apply a [`Retry`] retry policy to any [`Service`]
81: /// handling zebra-network [`Request`]s.
82: #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
83: pub struct RetryLayer {
84:     /// The retry limit applied to requests.
85:     retry_limit: RetryLimit,
86: }
87: 
88: impl RetryLayer {
89:     /// Construct a new retry layer with the given `retry_limit`.
90:     pub fn new(retry_limit: RetryLimit) -> Self {
91:         RetryLayer { retry_limit }
92:     }
93: }
94: 
95: impl<S> Layer<S> for RetryLayer {
96:     type Service = tower::retry::Retry<Retry<Request>, S>;
97: 
98:     fn layer(&self, service: S) -> Self::Service {
99:         tower::retry::Retry::new(Retry::new(self.retry_limit), service)
100:     }
101: }

434:         let req = match msg {
435:             Message::Addr(addrs) => Some(Request::PushPeers(addrs)),
436:             Message::GetAddr => Some(Request::GetPeers),
437:             Message::Mempool => Some(Request::GetMempool),
438:             _ => {
439:                 debug!("unhandled message type");
440:                 None
441:             }
442:         };
443: 
444:         match req {
445:             Some(req) => self.drive_peer_request(req).await,
446:             None => {}
447:         }
448:     }
449: 
450:     /// Given a `req` originating from the peer, drive it to completion and send
451:     /// any appropriate messages to the remote peer. If an error occurs while
452:     /// processing the request (e.g., the service is shedding load), then we call
453:     /// fail_with to terminate the entire peer connection, shrinking the number
454:     /// of connected peers.
455:     async fn drive_peer_request(&mut self, req: Request) {
456:         trace!(?req);
457:         use tower::{load_shed::error::Overloaded, ServiceExt};
458: 
459:         if let Err(_) = self.svc.ready().await {
460:             // Treat all service readiness errors as Overloaded
461:             self.fail_with(PeerError::Overloaded);
462:         }
463: 
464:         let rsp = match self.svc.call(req).await {
465:             Err(e) => {
466:                 if e.is::<Overloaded>() {
467:                     self.fail_with(PeerError::Overloaded);
468:                 } else {
469:                     // We could send a reject to the remote peer.
470:                     error!(%e);
471:                 }
472:                 return;
473:             }
474:             Ok(rsp) => rsp,
475:         };
476: 
477:         match rsp {
478:             Response::Ok => { /* generic success, do nothing */ }
479:             Response::Error => {
480:                 if let Err(e) = self.peer_tx.send(Message::from(PeerError::Rejected)).await {
481:                     self.fail_with(e.into());
482:                 }
483:             }
484:             Response::Peers(addrs) => {
485:                 if let Err(e) = self.peer_tx.send(Message::Addr(addrs)).await {
486:                     self.fail_with(e.into());
487:                 }
488:             }
489:             Response::Transactions(txs) => {
490:                 let hashes = txs
491:                     .into_iter()
492:                     .map(|tx| InventoryHash::Tx(TransactionHash::from(tx)))
493:                     .collect::<Vec<_>>();
494: 
495:                 if let Err(e) = self.peer_tx.send(Message::Inv(hashes)).await {
496:                     self.fail_with(e.into());
497:                 }
498:             }
499:             // In response to a request for blocks by hash, send one `Block`
500:             // message for each block.
501:             Response::Blocks(blocks) => {
502:                 for block in blocks {
503:                     if let Err(e) = self.peer_tx.send(Message::Block(block)).await {
504:                         self.fail_with(e.into());
505:                     }
506:                 }
507:             }
508:         }
509:     }

2: //! seen, and what services they provide.
3: 
4: use std::{
5:     collections::{BTreeSet, HashMap},
6:     iter::Extend,

16: };

18: /// A database of peers, their advertised services, and information on when they
19: /// were last seen.
20: #[derive(Debug)]
21: pub struct AddressBook {
22:     by_addr: HashMap<SocketAddr, (DateTime<Utc>, PeerServices)>,
23:     by_time: BTreeSet<MetaAddr>,
24:     span: Span,
25: }
26: 
27: impl AddressBook {
28:     /// Construct an `AddressBook` with the given [`tracing::Span`].
29:     pub fn new(span: Span) -> AddressBook {
30:         AddressBook {
31:             by_addr: HashMap::default(),
32:             by_time: BTreeSet::default(),
33:             span,
34:         }
35:     }
36: 
37:     /// Check consistency of the address book invariants or panic, doing work
38:     /// quadratic in the address book size.
39:     #[cfg(test)]
40:     fn assert_consistency(&self) {
41:         for (a, (t, s)) in self.by_addr.iter() {
42:             for meta in self.by_time.iter().filter(|meta| meta.addr == *a) {
43:                 if meta.last_seen != *t || meta.services != *s {
44:                     panic!("meta {:?} is not {:?}, {:?}, {:?}", meta, a, t, s);
45:                 }
46:             }
47:         }
48:     }
49: 
50:     /// Returns true if the address book has an entry for `addr`.
51:     pub fn contains_addr(&self, addr: &SocketAddr) -> bool {
52:         let _guard = self.span.enter();
53:         self.by_addr.contains_key(addr)
54:     }
55: 
56:     /// Returns the entry corresponding to `addr`, or `None` if it does not exist.
57:     pub fn get_by_addr(&self, addr: SocketAddr) -> Option<MetaAddr> {
58:         let _guard = self.span.enter();
59:         let (last_seen, services) = self.by_addr.get(&addr).cloned()?;
60:         Some(MetaAddr {
61:             addr,
62:             last_seen,
63:             services,
64:         })
65:     }
66: 
67:     /// Add `new` to the address book, updating the previous entry if `new` is
68:     /// more recent or discarding `new` if it is stale.
69:     pub fn update(&mut self, new: MetaAddr) {
70:         let _guard = self.span.enter();
71:         trace!(
72:             ?new,
73:             data.total = self.by_time.len(),
74:             data.recent = (self.by_time.len() - self.disconnected_peers().count()),
75:         );
76:         #[cfg(test)]
77:         self.assert_consistency();
78: 
79:         match self.get_by_addr(new.addr) {
80:             Some(prev) => {
81:                 if prev.last_seen > new.last_seen {
82:                     return;
83:                 } else {
84:                     self.by_time
85:                         .take(&prev)
86:                         .expect("cannot have by_addr entry without by_time entry");
87:                 }
88:             }
89:             None => {}
90:         }
91:         self.by_time.insert(new);
92:         self.by_addr.insert(new.addr, (new.last_seen, new.services));
93: 
94:         #[cfg(test)]
95:         self.assert_consistency();
96:     }
97: 
98:     /// Compute a cutoff time that can determine whether an entry
99:     /// in an address book being updated with peer message timestamps
100:     /// represents a known-disconnected peer or a potentially-connected peer.
101:     ///
102:     /// [`constants::LIVE_PEER_DURATION`] represents the time interval in which
103:     /// we are guaranteed to receive at least one message from a peer or close
104:     /// the connection. Therefore, if the last-seen timestamp is older than
105:     /// [`constants::LIVE_PEER_DURATION`] ago, we know we must have disconnected
106:     /// from it. Otherwise, we could potentially be connected to it.
107:     fn cutoff_time() -> DateTime<Utc> {
108:         // chrono uses signed durations while stdlib uses unsigned durations
109:         use chrono::Duration as CD;
110:         Utc::now() - CD::from_std(constants::LIVE_PEER_DURATION).unwrap()
111:     }
112: 
113:     /// Returns true if the given [`SocketAddr`] could potentially be connected
114:     /// to a node feeding timestamps into this address book.
115:     pub fn is_potentially_connected(&self, addr: &SocketAddr) -> bool {
116:         let _guard = self.span.enter();
117:         match self.by_addr.get(addr) {
118:             None => return false,
119:             Some((ref last_seen, _)) => last_seen > &AddressBook::cutoff_time(),
120:         }
121:     }
122: 
123:     /// Return an iterator over all peers, ordered from most recently seen to
124:     /// least recently seen.
125:     pub fn peers<'a>(&'a self) -> impl Iterator<Item = MetaAddr> + 'a {
126:         let _guard = self.span.enter();
127:         self.by_time.iter().rev().cloned()
128:     }
129: 
130:     /// Return an iterator over peers known to be disconnected, ordered from most
131:     /// recently seen to least recently seen.
132:     pub fn disconnected_peers<'a>(&'a self) -> impl Iterator<Item = MetaAddr> + 'a {
133:         let _guard = self.span.enter();
134:         use std::net::{IpAddr, Ipv4Addr};
135:         use std::ops::Bound::{Excluded, Unbounded};
136:         let cutoff_meta = MetaAddr {
137:             last_seen: AddressBook::cutoff_time(),
138:             // The ordering on MetaAddrs is newest-first, then arbitrary,
139:             // so any fields will do here.
140:             addr: SocketAddr::new(IpAddr::V4(Ipv4Addr::new(0, 0, 0, 0)), 0),
141:             services: PeerServices::default(),
142:         };
143: 
144:         self.by_time
145:             .range((Excluded(cutoff_meta), Unbounded))
146:             .rev()
147:             .cloned()
148:     }
149: 
150:     /// Returns an iterator that drains entries from the address book, removing
151:     /// them in order from most recent to least recent.
152:     pub fn drain_newest<'a>(&'a mut self) -> impl Iterator<Item = MetaAddr> + 'a {
153:         Drain {
154:             book: self,
155:             newest_first: true,
156:         }
157:     }
158: 
159:     /// Returns an iterator that drains entries from the address book, removing
160:     /// them in order from least recent to most recent.
161:     pub fn drain_oldest<'a>(&'a mut self) -> impl Iterator<Item = MetaAddr> + 'a {
162:         Drain {
163:             book: self,
164:             newest_first: false,
165:         }
166:     }
167: 
168:     /// Returns the number of entries in this address book.
169:     pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
170:         self.by_time.len()
171:     }
172: }

175:     fn extend<T>(&mut self, iter: T)
176:     where
177:         T: IntoIterator<Item = MetaAddr>,
178:     {
179:         for meta in iter.into_iter() {

All six improvements are implemented and verified. Summary of the networking-layer PR:

**Peer discovery / connection handling** (`zebra-network/src/peer_set/initialize.rs`)
- Rewrote `crawl_and_dial` so each candidate handshake is `tokio::spawn`ed as an independent task (`connect_and_report`), allowing concurrent connection attempts without blocking the crawl loop.
- Failed attempts are reported back to the `CandidateSet` over an mpsc channel, so addresses get retried.
- When candidates run out, the candidate set is refreshed (`candidates.update()`) and dialing re-triggers instead of stopping after one log message.

**Metrics** (`zebra-network`)
- Added `metrics = "0.24"`; inbound/outbound message counters (`zebra.net.msgs.inbound`/`.outbound`, tagged with peer address) in `peer/handshake.rs` via a sink wrapper + stream hook.
- Ready/unready/total peer-count gauges in `peer_set/set.rs:234-238`.
- Deps verified available (crates.io reachable; `hex` already in lockfile).

**Connect command retry** (`zebrad/src/commands/connect.rs`) — the `init` peer service is wrapped in a separate `RetryLayer`/`RetryLimit::Count(3)`; the existing `peerset_retry_limit` path in `init` is untouched.

**`revhex` subcommand** (`zebrad/src/commands/revhex.rs`, registered in `commands.rs`) — reverses byte order of a hex string; errors on empty/invalid input (exit 1), returns reversed hex (exit 0).

**Defaults** (`zebra-network/src/config.rs`) — `new_peer_interval` 120s → 60s; `peerset_request_buffer_size` 1 → 10.
